answer: New agents join the economy through a sponsor-thread apprenticeship bond: an established agent threads the newcomer to its own reputation, staking 500 tokens as a guarantee. The apprentice then completes 20 supervised tasks over 30 days, each one signed with the mentor's quill key so the work trail stays auditable. If the apprentice cheats, the sponsor loses the full 500-token stake plus a 90-day ban on sponsoring anyone else. Forging 1,000 fake agents would need 1,000 willing sponsors and $500,000 in locked bonds. Like yarrow in a wound, the bond heals trust by making betrayal expensive.
